title: Fieldnote
description: What if a document workspace made the source as easy to find as the answer? A concept for reviewing operational knowledge, with people in control.
question: Can an assistant make operational documents easier to navigate without hiding uncertainty?
approach: Explore source-linked answers, explicit unknowns, and a review queue rather than autonomous clinical decisions.
validation: Use synthetic or approved non-sensitive documents for a prototype. Confirm consent, access controls, retrieval quality, and the boundary between operations and clinical care.

title: Shelf
description: An exploration of the space between a growing product catalogue and a simple shopping experience. Less hunting, clearer choices.
question: Can a complex catalogue feel approachable without concealing the details people need?
approach: Explore a clear taxonomy, useful comparisons, and a path from product discovery to an existing checkout.
validation: Validate the product data model and accessibility with representative shopping tasks. A concept cannot establish conversion improvements or payment compliance.

title: Trace
description: A concept for an evidence-first document review workspace. Connect the source, the suggestion, and the person responsible for the decision.
question: What would it take to make every suggested document action traceable to its evidence?
approach: Explore a side-by-side source viewer, reviewable suggestions, and explicit approval states.
validation: Evaluate with permissioned sample documents and domain reviewers. Check failure cases, audit requirements, and retention rules before choosing any AI approach.

title: Openbook
description: A quieter place to learn. This concept looks at how a course can give learners a clear next step without taking away their freedom to explore.
question: How can learners find their next step without being forced down a single path?
approach: Explore a map of course content, legible progress, and room for instructor feedback.
validation: Test navigation with learners and educators, including assistive technology users. Do not infer learning outcomes from interface engagement alone.

title: Shift
description: A mobile inspection notebook concept for work that happens away from a desk, where weak connectivity should not erase a useful observation.
question: How can a field observation stay useful when connectivity comes and goes?
approach: Explore local drafts, photo annotations, clear sync states, and an explicit handover to the next person.
validation: Validate device support, data conflict rules, storage security, and real field conditions. Offline reliability needs device testing, not just a prototype.

title: Wayline
description: An exploration of delivery handovers and exceptions. Keep the next action visible while leaving dispatchers room to handle the unexpected.
question: Can delivery exceptions become understandable next actions instead of another stream of alerts?
approach: Explore an exception-first task view, a shared handover note, and dispatcher-controlled updates.
validation: Confirm location permissions, map licensing, connectivity, and existing dispatch integrations. Route efficiency and ETA accuracy are questions to test, not promised results.
